goal.title: Two-week backpacking trip through Portugal and Spain

conversation.content: I want to do a two-week backpacking trip through Portugal and Spain starting May 1st. Total budget $2,500 including flights. I prefer trains and hostels. I can spend maybe 3 hours a week on planning.

expected_output.message_to_user:
Your trip route has 3 stages: lock in the big decisions (route, flights), sort documents and money, then plan the days. It fits in about 3 hours a week and finishes a week before departure.
Entry rules for Spain and Portugal depend on your passport and may have changed recently, so the first task is to check them on official sources — I haven't assumed anything about visas or travel authorisations.
Flights are the biggest single cost, so they're booked early; day-by-day details come later.

goal.title: Two-week backpacking trip through Portugal and Spain
goal.desired_outcome: A booked and budgeted 14-day trip starting May 1st, travelling by train and staying in hostels.
success_criteria: Flights and first two nights booked

journey.strategy_summary: Decide the route and book flights early, confirm documents and money, then plan accommodation and days in order of how fast they sell out.

milestones.title: Documents and money sorted
success_criteria: Entry requirements confirmed for your passport
Card or cash plan for euros ready

milestones.title: Trip fully planned
success_criteria: Day plan and budget sheet complete

nodes.title: Check entry requirements for your passport

task.title: Check Schengen entry requirements for your passport on 2 official sources
task.description: On your government's travel advice page and the official EU or Spanish/Portuguese government pages, check whether you need a visa or a travel authorisation for a 14-day stay, plus passport validity rules.
task.why_it_matters: If an authorisation or visa is needed, it has lead times that shape the whole schedule.
task.expected_result: A short note listing each requirement, its source link and the date checked.

methods.instructions: Submit each requirement with the official link and the date you checked.
The navigator opens each linked official page and checks that it states the recorded requirement.

pass_criteria: Requirements recorded with official source links
Each linked page confirms the recorded requirement
verification_protocol.rationale: The note is the user's summary; confidence comes from checking every cited official page, not from the note itself.

task.title: Draft a 4–5 city route with train legs and nights per city
task.description: Choose 4–5 cities, the order, nights in each and the train connection between them. Keep at least 3 nights in the first and last city to absorb flight delays.
task.why_it_matters: The route determines which airports to fly into and out of, which is the biggest cost decision.
task.expected_result: A route table with cities, nights and train legs.

acceptance_criteria: Every leg has a train option

pass_criteria: Route totals 14 nights with a train connection for each leg
verification_protocol.rationale: The route table is the deliverable itself, so nights and legs are checked directly; train availability is only confirmed later during booking, hence medium.

task.title: Compare 3 flight options and book one that keeps flights under 40% of budget
task.description: Compare round-trip and open-jaw options (fly into the first city, out of the last) on at least two booking sites, then book one.
task.why_it_matters: Flights are the largest cost; booking months ahead usually keeps them within budget.
task.expected_result: A booking confirmation and a comparison of 3 options.

methods.instructions: Upload the booking confirmation (hide payment details) and the 3-option comparison.

pass_criteria: Confirmed booking matching the trip dates
verification_protocol.rationale: A booking confirmation is direct evidence.

nodes.title: Apply for any required travel authorisation or visa
Set up a budget sheet and a no-foreign-fee payment option
One-page day plan per city with 2 food markets each

external_claims.claim: Entry requirements (visa, travel authorisation, passport validity) for the user's passport.
Train routes and prices between the chosen cities.

decision_summary.what_changed: Created a 3-stage planning route that ends one week before departure.
decision_summary.why: Entry rules and flights have the longest lead times and the biggest budget impact, so they come first.
decision_summary.impact: About 3 hours a week; flights capped at 40% of the $2,500 budget.

contrastive.critique: Plans 12 hours a week when the user has 3, and sets the planning milestone after the departure date.

output.message_to_user: Here's an intensive planning schedule so everything is perfect!

goal.title: Two-week backpacking trip through Portugal and Spain

decision_summary.why: More planning means a better trip.
